security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown inline code, file names, CSS, and HTML examples. I confirmed only the third-party CDN script examples, explicit npx HyperFrames commands, and the background CLI child-process fallback as real operational risks. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, malware logic, or hidden data collection.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer a local bundled GSAP dependency, or clearly document that generated compositions may require third-party network access.
Require explicit user approval before running npx hyperframes commands and prefer a pinned local project dependency when possible.
Gate background workers behind explicit approval, constrain their workspace, and record the exact commands and log paths used.

content.value_statement: HyperFrames projects can break when timing, media, or sub-composition rules are missed. This skill gives agents a concise contract for render-ready HTML video compositions.
actual_capabilities: Explains standalone and sub-composition root structures.
Documents data-* timing attributes, clip classes, tracks, and durations.
Describes deterministic animation rules for seekable video rendering.
Shows how to wire media, variables, and sub-composition hosts.
Provides validation steps for lint, inspect, snapshot, preview, and render workflows.
Covers Tailwind v4 patterns for browser-runtime compositions.
limitations: Does not include the HyperFrames CLI command reference itself.
Does not provide animation runtime details beyond the core contract.
Does not generate final media assets or run renders by itself.
Requires a compatible HyperFrames project and tooling to validate output.

use_cases.title: Create a New Composition
use_cases.description: Use the core contract to create a sized HTML composition with clips, tracks, and one seekable timeline.

use_cases.title: Repair Render Bugs
use_cases.description: Check timing, root sizing, media placement, and id naming when a composition previews differently from render.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Modular Scenes
use_cases.description: Plan host slots, sub-composition templates, shared audio, and validation gates for multi-scene video projects.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Minimal Composition
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single-scene render.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use hyperframes-core to create a minimal standalone HyperFrames composition for a five-second title scene. Follow the root sizing, clip timing, and timeline rules.

prompt_templates.title: Check an Existing Project
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic review of a composition before validation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this HyperFrames project against hyperframes-core. Report issues with root size, data attributes, media placement, tracks, ids, and deterministic animation.

prompt_templates.title: Design Modular Scenes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use hyperframes-core to plan a modular HyperFrames project with three scenes and shared audio. Define the host slots, sub-composition ids, timing, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Render Differences
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced troubleshooting for preview and render mismatch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use hyperframes-core to diagnose why preview and render differ in this project. Focus on deterministic state, root backgrounds, media ownership, timeline registration, and sub-composition transport rules.

output_examples.input: A request for a six-second product intro composition.
output_examples.output: The agent outlines a sized standalone composition, one root timeline, timed clips, safe media placement, and validation commands to run after review.

output_examples.input: A project where a sub-composition renders blank.
output_examples.output: The agent identifies likely template transport, id matching, root styling, or duplicate media id issues and lists focused checks.

output_examples.input: A Tailwind-based scene with dynamic classes.
output_examples.output: The agent recommends static class tokens, CSS variables, fixed viewport sizing, and seekable animation controlled outside Tailwind transitions.

best_practices: Read the relevant reference file before changing composition structure.
Keep timelines seekable, deterministic, and registered under the exact composition id.
Run validation and visual snapshot checks before rendering final video.
anti_patterns: Do not wrap a standalone composition root in a template.
Do not place video or audio inside a sub-composition template.
Do not use clocks, unseeded randomness, network state, or input state during render.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps agents build deterministic HyperFrames HTML projects that can preview, validate, and render as video.

faq.question: Does it replace the HyperFrames CLI documentation?
faq.answer: No. It gives the composition contract and points to CLI validation steps, but command details live elsewhere.

faq.question: Can it work with Tailwind?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents Tailwind v4 browser-runtime patterns and warns against dynamic render-critical class names.

faq.question: Does it support sub-compositions?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains host slots, templates, id matching, variables, and validation checks for modular scenes.

faq.question: Will it render videos automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can guide the project structure and validation workflow, but rendering requires approved external tooling.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
